problem_statement: The kernel should support platforms whose system timer clock rate can change at runtime. When such a platform applies a new clock frequency it must publish it through a runtime update hook, and the system timer frequency returned by sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec() must reflect the newly published value. The hook must accept a new non-zero frequency, treat a request for the current frequency as a no-op, and ignore a request for zero (leaving the frequency unchanged).

problem_statement_fixed:
The kernel should support platforms whose system timer clock rate can change at runtime. When such a platform applies a new clock frequency it must publish it through a runtime update hook, and the system timer frequency returned by sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec() must reflect the newly published value. The hook must accept a new non-zero frequency, treat a request for the current frequency as a no-op, and ignore a request for zero (leaving the frequency unchanged).

The hook is a function named z_sys_clock_hw_cycles_per_sec_update(uint32_t new_hz) and must be declared in the header <zephyr/drivers/timer/system_timer.h>. It shall only be available when the Kconfig option CONFIG_SYSTEM_CLOCK_HW_CYCLES_PER_SEC_RUNTIME_UPDATE is enabled.
